column3: “Sought the face of the LORD” is rendered “sought the presence of the LORD,” and “house of bloods” as “bloody house.”
NASB puts the explanation in parentheses; “sworn an oath” is rendered “made a covenant,” and “strike down” as “kill.”
“Make amends” is rendered “make atonement,” and NASB adds “that you may.”
“Not to us silver and gold” is rendered “We have no concern of silver or gold.”
“Made an end of us” is rendered “consumed us”; NASB joins the clause to verse 6.
“Descendants” is rendered “sons,” and “impale” as “hang.”
“Had compassion on” is rendered “spared.”
The Hebrew reads “Michal”; NASB has “Merab,” as in some manuscripts (compare 1 Sam 18:19).
“Impaled” is rendered “hanged.”
“Water was poured out on them” is rendered “it rained on them.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB links it to verse 12.
“Citizens” is rendered “men,” and “hung up” as “hanged.”
“The impaled men” is rendered “those who had been hanged.”
“God was entreated” is rendered “God was moved by entreaty.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“The Raphah” is rendered “the giant”; NASB supplies “shekels” and “sword” (the Hebrew has only “a new [thing]”). “Said to strike down” becomes “intended to kill.”
NASB renders “and not you will extinguish” as “that you may not extinguish.”
“The Raphah” is rendered “the giant.”
The Hebrew reads that Elhanan struck down “Goliath the Gittite”; NASB follows it (compare 1 Chr 20:5, “the brother of Goliath”).
“Six and six” is rendered “six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot”; “the Raphah” is rendered “the giant.”
“Taunted” is rendered “defied,” and the written Hebrew “Shimeah” as “Shimei” (reading tradition).
“The Raphah” is rendered “the giant.”
